statement: The British Museum catalogs an Aksumite copper-alloy coin (1989,0518.87) with a Greek cross on the reverse and an anonymous ruler, giving a broad circa 340–540 CE production interval; the iconographic evidence supports Christian symbolism in Aksumite minting but does not independently date Ezana's own conversion.

sources.citation: British Museum Collections Online, anonymous Aksumite coin, 1989,0518.87, https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/C_1989-0518-87
sources.author: British Museum
sources.access_note: Indexed museum record names the Greek cross and approximate date 340–540; direct page returned HTTP 403. Artifact and coin-series dating not checked from primary numismatic edition.

does_not_demonstrate: This broad object date cannot fix Ezana's conversion year.
The anonymous coin should not be misattributed to Ezana.
Christian royal iconography does not establish exclusive Christian practice throughout Aksum.
adversarial_counter: The broad 200-year museum date and anonymous attribution limit the chronological conclusion to use of a cross motif sometime within the cataloged period.
notes: Metropolitan Museum's contextual essay 'African Christianity in Ethiopia' independently interprets cross-bearing Aksumite coinage but is not a substitute for the specific museum inventory record.
